title: Halting under composition of simulations
statement: Let $N$ and $M$ be nondeterministic Turing machines with Boolean symbols, respectively with $K$ and $K'$ work tapes and state sets $S$ and $S'$, on a fixed Boolean input. Let $\varphi$ map configurations of $N$ to configurations of $M$. Suppose that whenever a configuration $c$ of $N$ is nonhalting, one step of $M$ from $\varphi(c)$ under any choice bit equals the image under $\varphi$ of the corresponding step of $N$. Suppose also that there is an $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, from the image of any halting configuration of $N$, every choice word of length $m$ leads $M$ to a halting configuration. Then, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and configuration $c$ of $N$, if every choice word of length $n$ leads $N$ from $c$ to a halting configuration, every choice word of length $n+m$ leads $M$ from $\varphi(c)$ to a halting configuration.
